claims.text: The FeNiCrMn HEA has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The FeNiCrMn HEA has a microstructure typical of as-cast or thermomechanically processed high-entropy alloys.
In-situ tensile testing combined with full-field strain mapping will reveal localized microstructural deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation interactions and nano-twinning are localized deformation mechanisms that underpin the mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn.
Controlled tensile loading at multiple strain rates with concurrent DIC and periodic SEM/EBSD observations is an appropriate experimental method.
Grain boundaries, dislocation networks, and nano-twin formations are structural mediators of deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Microstructural heterogeneities mediate localized deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Microstructural heterogeneities activate dislocation interactions and potentially nano-twinning.
Dislocation interactions and nano-twinning contribute to improved ductility and strength.
The proposed experiments will produce heterogeneously distributed high-strain regions.
High-strain regions will correlate with specific microstructural features.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit an enhanced capacity to accommodate plasticity compared with conventional alloys.
Conventional alloys or other studied HEAs are expected to show a more uniform strain distribution under similar loading conditions.
Conventional alloys or other studied HEAs are expected to exhibit less pronounced local deformation mechanisms under similar loading conditions.
The hypothesized deformation effects may be less discernible outside the tested strain-rate regimes.
Processing-induced material inhomogeneity may mask the deformation mechanisms of interest.
